result.question: Model Mimir Labs year by year (5 years): revenue/MRR build, burn incl. COGS, runway, whether/when the pre-seed closes, and time to founder becoming a millionaire (paper vs liquid).

report.question: Model Mimir Labs year by year (5 years): revenue/MRR build, burn incl. COGS, runway, whether/when the pre-seed closes, and time to founder becoming a millionaire (paper vs liquid).

prediction.headline: Pre-seed never actually closes in the deterministic ledger — interest soft-circles and 'commits' on paper, but no capital is ever injected (raise_injected:false all 5 years); the business instead bootstraps to ~$97K ARR on services + Yggdrasil cash, and the founder ends neither paper nor liquid millionaire.
prediction.likely_lead: Ben Franklin Technology Partners (C&N PA) anchoring a small priced/SAFE round (~$250K), with Robin Hood Ventures / Schematic / 640 Oxford as the realistic angel-to-pre-seed syndicate at the TRUE traction level (~$65–97K ARR)
prediction.terms_estimate: $300–500K priced at ~$3.5–4M pre-money (founder repriced down from the $5M ask); min-viable close $300K. NOTE: the persona checks (DataTribe $3M, Work-Bench $1.5M, Schematic/Ironspring/Differential $500K each) are anchored to a hallucinated $13.4M-ARR projection, NOT the real ledger — at true ~$65K ARR those checks do not materialize.

founder_millionaire.note: PAPER never crosses $1M in the real ledger: no priced round is ever injected (raise_injected:false every year), so there is no marked valuation. Founder holds 100% of a company at ~$97K ARR — at even a generous 8x ARR mark that is ~$775K, still under $1M, and that mark requires a close that never happens. LIQUID never crosses $1M either: ARR stays far below the $255K draw gate all 5 years, so the founder draws $0 salary and the slow (salary − lifestyle) accrual path never even starts; there is no acquisition or secondary. The year-log narrative claiming a Year-3 paper-millionaire and a Year-5 liquid trigger is built on the projection ARR (~$2.36M / ~$13.4M), which the authoritative ledger contradicts by ~140x. On the real numbers, neither crossing occurs inside the window.

financial_outlook.one_liner: A capital-efficient, 89%-blended-margin solo bootstrap that turns cash-flow positive in Year 2 and ends Year 5 at ~$97K ARR with ~$88K in the bank and 100% founder ownership — but the priced round and the millionaire crossings both live in a projection that the ledger never realizes.

report.causal_narrative: Year 1 runs underwater from month one ($0 opening cash) as ~$9K of early services/Norn revenue can't cover ~$45K of fixed OpEx, ending at -$37K cash and just $15.6K ARR — the solo-founder engineering constraint and open critical blockers (YGGDATA-258 data-loss, no email, broken business-flows, no SOC 2) cap how fast paid logos convert. A lumpy services year (Ratatosk/Ragnarok cash-on-delivery plus a Yggdrasil pilot) lifts Year-2 revenue to ~$56K and flips net positive (+$5.7K), but recurring ARR barely moves because almost none of that revenue is recurring. Years 3–5 grind the recurring base from 1 to 3 active tenants, ARR creeping $31K → $65K → $97K, with net turning durably positive in Year 4 (+$51K) and Year 5 (+$76K) as fixed OpEx stays flat at ~$45K and gross margin holds near 90%. The pre-seed is the central illusion: investor personas escalate to 'committed' with large indicative checks, but those commitments are pinned to a $13.4M-ARR projection that the ledger never produces, so no capital is ever injected and the founder funds lifestyle externally while drawing $0. The result is a real, healthy micro-SaaS that the founder owns outright — but at ~$97K ARR it is two orders of magnitude short of the traction that would make either the priced round or the millionaire thresholds real.
caveats: The persona table and year-log are internally inconsistent with the authoritative ledger by roughly 140x on ARR ($13.4M projected vs ~$97K actual). I treated the LEDGER as authoritative per instructions; every investor 'committed' stance and the Year-3/Year-5 millionaire claims rest on the inflated projection and should be discounted heavily.

raise_injected is false in all five ledger years and end-cash is funded entirely by operating revenue, so despite 'committed_capital' rising to $7.15M, NO external capital actually hits the treasury in the model. The pre-seed effectively does not close in the deterministic run; my 0.35 close probability reflects real-world plausibility of a small BFTP-anchored round at true traction, not the ledger.

The founder draws $0 all 5 years because ARR never reaches the $255K gate — lifestyle ($4,500/mo) is assumed externally funded with no liquid drag. If that external support fails, the negative-cash Years 1–3 are not survivable without a bridge.

Opening cash is $0, so Years 1 and 3 end negative; the model implicitly assumes vendors/founder absorb the shortfall (or a small services-cash buffer), otherwise the company is technically insolvent in those years.
Blended gross margin (~0.89) is my revenue-weighted estimate across the 5 ledger years; individual years range 0.82–0.92 depending on services mix.

Liquid millionaire via the organic path is mathematically impossible in-window even if the draw gate were hit: max (salary − lifestyle) is roughly ($185K − $54K) = ~$131K/yr, so ~8+ years of full drawing would be needed — only an acquisition or secondary could do it inside 5 years, and neither occurs in the ledger.

Critical product blockers (data-loss YGGDATA-258, SOC 2 not ready) gate enterprise signatures; the slow tenant ramp (0→3) in the ledger is consistent with those gates NOT clearing fast, which is the more believable path than the projection's enterprise stampede.

coalitions.name: BFTP-anchored capital syndicate
coalitions.note: The only door that plausibly writes a small check at ~$65–97K ARR. BFTP econ-dev thesis + warm regional intros; this is where a real $250–500K pre-seed would actually originate.

coalitions.name: Thesis-fit institutional VCs (projection-dependent)
coalitions.note: These large checks ($500K–$3M) are contingent on the projection traction the ledger never reaches. At real ARR they revert to 'watching,' so I exclude them from the realistic close.

coalitions.name: Design-partner / customer flywheel
coalitions.note: The real revenue engine. The MTO/ETO enterprise deal stays gated on SOC 2 Type 1 + data-loss fix, which is why ARR stays small.

coalitions.name: Accelerator (window closed)
coalitions.note: $0 indicative; entry window framed as closed in the persona read regardless of which ARR is true.

swing_factors.factor: Reconciling projection ARR vs ledger ARR
swing_factors.why: Every investor commitment and both millionaire crossings hinge on $13.4M ARR; the ledger says ~$97K. Whether the company is actually on the projection curve or the ledger curve flips the entire outcome from 'priced round + paper millionaire' to 'self-funded micro-SaaS, no close, no crossing.'

swing_factors.factor: Clearing critical blockers (YGGDATA-258 data-loss + SOC 2 Type 1)
swing_factors.why: These are hard signing gates for enterprise manufacturers. The ledger's slow 0→3 tenant ramp implies they clear slowly; fixing them earlier is the single biggest lever on recurring ARR and therefore on hitting the $255K draw gate.

swing_factors.factor: Whether a small BFTP-anchored round actually injects capital
swing_factors.why: raise_injected stays false in the ledger. A real $300–500K close would fund the customer-facing engineer hire, relax the solo-founder capacity constraint, and accelerate the tenant ramp — the difference between $97K and several-hundred-K ARR by Year 5.

swing_factors.factor: External lifestyle funding holding through Years 1–3
swing_factors.why: Founder draws $0 and ends Years 1 and 3 cash-negative. The model only survives because lifestyle is externally covered with no liquid drag; if that fails, a bridge is mandatory or the company stalls.

The ONLY in-window path to liquid-millionaire (acquisition cash portion 0.7). It never fires in the ledger (acquired:false all years), so liquid stays null; a corp-dev event is the binary switch that would change that.

paper.basis: ownership × marked valuation (priced round pre-money $4000000, or acquisition price). ILLIQUID.

liquid.basis: acquisition cash-out + founder secondary + slow (salary − lifestyle) accrual once drawing (ARR ≥ $255K). Lifestyle externally funded until draw → no drag, no debt. A fundraise yields $0 liquid.
